family: The single total certificate-prefix language specified in proof.md and family.py. For actual length N, choose k as the least prime at least the least positive B with B^5>32*N^3; read k input bits as the lower coefficients of a monic degree-k polynomial Q over F_2, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, and evaluate the descending-power BK symmetric polynomial on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding, r=ceil((N-k)/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)). Output 0 for N=0 or the explicit failed guards in proof.md. The output is the constant coefficient in F_2[Z]/Q. All k prefix bits are included in N; Q is input, not advice.
theorem: For the single total uniform polynomial-time certificate-prefix family defined in proof.md and family.py, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-3k-8d_N+7 for all sufficiently large integer N, where W=r(r+3)/2, H=(t-1)(t+2)/2, A0=(t-1)k-H-(r-t+1), L=floor(t*k/(t+1)-t/2), q=floor(L/t), a=L-t*q, d_N=1+W+max(A0,r*q+a), k=O(N^(3/5)), and d_N=O(N^(4/5)). The additional k>=t(t+1)/2 holds eventually. At every sufficiently large length, d_N<=d_boundary=1+W+max(A0,floor(r(k-1)/(t+1))); when r=t^2 and t>=3, d_boundary-d_N>=floor(t^2*(t-1)/(2*(t+1)))>=2. Infinitely many such actual lengths occur because k(N) is nondecreasing, r(N+1)<=r(N)+1, and r(N) tends to infinity. Every prefix bit is essential at sufficiently large lengths; fixing an accepted prefix with nonconstant payload removes at least k gates in the strengthened signed-wire/output-literal model. Consequently liminf over ALL integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N>=4 in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length N. Moreover (3k+8d_N-7)/(4k+8d_old-5) tends to1/2, where d_old=floor(kr/t)+kt+r(r+1)+1; this compares proved remainder certificates, not actual circuit complexities. The supplied generic additive-seven theorem for d>=3 uses exactly the four normalized R84 refutations and complete Q7 read-once formula coverage executed by audit.py, with complete normalization and unrestricted-sharing transfer in elimination.md. The exact integer-balancing argument in disperser.md Section13 gives d_N<=d_sharp=1+W+max(A0,floor(r*(2k-t-1)/(2*(t+1)))) for every tuple in scope; at N=565701 the respective thresholds are56458 and56528. No strict improvement over d_sharp at all lengths is asserted.
